domain: environmental regulation - federal impact-assessment lifecycle outcome (Canadian Impact Assessment Registry)
prediction_question: For a project assessment posted to the Canadian Impact Assessment Registry, at its registry start date, will the assessment process terminate before any determination or decision is issued (proponent withdrawal / process termination), rather than run to a determination?
prediction_time: The assessment's registry start date (published per project on the registry page and in the MapServer layer as start_date). Features available at that instant: the inventory attributes published with the posting (project category, province, responsible authority(ies), location type, coordinates, description text, start date). The terminal state and its dated event (Latest update line: termination date, or Notice-of-Determination date + outcome wording) and the layer's current project_state_en/updated_at are post-hoc label sources and never ship as features. The registry is a live current archive: no historical vintages of pages are published, so the task is retrospective-within-current-archive, anchored on the dated events the current pages preserve; it cannot claim historical operational availability.
target_definition: Binary: the assessment's terminal state is 'Terminated' (MapServer layer 2 membership; registry page 'Assessment status: Terminated' plus a dated termination line in 'Latest update', e.g. proj 81027 'January 18, 2022 - The assessment process has been terminated') vs 'Completed' with a dated determination (e.g. proj 84411 'August 29, 2023 - ... determined that the project is not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects'). Label source columns: project_state_en, the page Latest-update text/date and Assessment status - all excluded from shipped features. Assessments still 'In progress' at fetch time are censored and must be handled by an explicit censoring rule, not dropped silently.

split_strategy: Temporal by registry start year. Volume era measured 2019+ (the IAA came into force 2019-08; pre-2019 rows in the layer are sparse backfill: 2006-2018 totals about 200 rows across 13 years). Measured starts/terminal counts per start year (state at 2026-10-30): 2019 215/16, 2020 836/48, 2021 968/51, 2022 907/47, 2023 956/48, 2024 917/32, 2025 944/29, 2026 650/7 (in-progress shares 5%, 8.5%, 9.4%, 12.2%, 15.7%, 17.6%, 22.0%, 55.1% - recent cohorts heavily right-censored). Candidate windows train 2019-2022 (2,926 starts / 162 terminal, 5.5%), eval 2023-2024 (1,873 / 80, 4.3%), holdout 2025-2026 (1,594 / 36, 2.3% BUT censored) - a holdout this recent needs an explicit censoring rule (e.g. fixed horizon from start date with unresolved rows excluded by rule, or push the holdout back once terminal-event lag is measured); pre-2019 rows usable only as documented partial backfill. Both classes present every year 2019-2026.

measurements.mapserver_probe_2026_10_30: Service info + per-layer counts + 8-record samples per layer (fields listed in sources). Total 6,600 projects: Completed 5,079, In progress 1,173, Terminated 348 (5.3%).
measurements.full_layer_fetch_2026_10_30: All 6,600 attribute rows (project_id, project_cat_en, province_codes, start_date, project_state_en; no geometry): 9 requests, 1,010,024 bytes, 6.58 s wall clock on the coordinator container. Retained probe script probe/iaac_layer_probe.py.
measurements.registry_page_samples_2026_10_30: 4 pages via extraction backend: 81027 Terminated (dated termination line 2022-01-18; non-designated project on federal lands), 84411 Completed (dated determination 2023-08-29, outcome wording 'not likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects'; clean text 149.8 KB mostly 'nearby assessments' nav noise), 80175 Completed designated CEAA-2012 project (key-documents table: Notice of Commencement 2019-07-05, EA Decision Statement 2021-01-11; 8.6 KB), 87425 In progress (dated latest update 2024-04-17, key-documents table with dates; 12.2 KB). Dated terminal events verified for 3/3 terminal-or-completed samples; sample size too small to generalize - the share of pages with parseable dated terminal events across the full cohort is the named next measurement.
measurements.novelty_search_preliminary_2026_10_30: Web search (queries: 'machine learning predicting environmental impact assessment outcome Canada decisions dataset', plus browsing of top results): no ML-ready benchmark or dataset found for predicting Canadian Impact Assessment Registry outcomes; results were CO2-emissions/LCA ML noise plus one Tandfonline review of AI-in-EIA literature (no registry-outcome task). A 2024 review of AI in EIA surfaced no outcome-prediction benchmark. Formal check-novelty.py with recorded verdict deferred until the bounded page-sample resolves extraction feasibility (investigating status).
measurements.cost_unknown_page_extraction: Per-page extraction cost at cohort scale (6,600 pages) NOT yet measured - named as the next bounded measurement before any ready verdict.

next_action: Bounded stratified sample of ~60-100 registry pages (states x start-years 2019-2026) on the coordinator or a worker: measure (a) share of pages exposing a dated, machine-parseable terminal event line (generalizing the 3/3 sample), (b) per-page fetch cost (bytes, seconds) and the total for 6,600 pages, (c) the determination-outcome wording mix - how often 'likely to cause significant adverse environmental effects' appears (decides whether the substantively richer label is ever frequent enough to be a secondary column or its own task; expected rare), (d) whether the 'All records' exploration view or the registry listing offers a bulk export that would replace per-page scraping. Then run scripts/check-novelty.py with recorded queries and a verdict. Timing contract needs the measured terminal-event lag distribution (start -> termination/determination) to fix the censoring rule and the holdout boundary. All cohort-scale extraction is a worker prerequisite, not coordinator work. NO construction was started in this session.
